q8.answer: Session state lives in a single shared Redis, under keys sess:<sha256(id)> (a hash with user_id, created_at, expires_at). Every app instance gets the cookie's session ID, hashes it and looks up that key in Redis, so any instance can serve any request.

q9.answer: Failures are kept in Redis in a sorted set fail:<lowercase email> of attempt timestamps. A Lua script on each failure removes entries older than 10 minutes, adds the new one and counts the rest, so the window is a sliding one based on the Redis server clock. At a count of 5 it sets lock:<email> with a 15-minute TTL.

q10.answer: One atomic step reads sess:<hash>. If the key exists and now is before created_at + 12h (using the Redis clock), it resets the key's TTL to min(30 min, created_at + 12h - now). So it compares now against created_at + 12h, and it writes back a refreshed TTL, which restarts the idle clock and never goes past the cap.

q11.answer: The browser gets a 503 "Service temporarily unavailable, please try again" page, with no session cookie set and no redirect to /dashboard. In the case where Redis is down, the lockout check fails first, so the password is not even checked. For a failure on session creation after the password check, the same fail-closed 503 applies, but I did not separately spell out that exact sequence.

q12.answer: Redis does it itself through key TTLs, with lazy deletion on access plus its background expiry sweep. No cron job or cleanup code is needed. The app also does a DEL of a key it finds past the 12-hour cap.
